price_note: Seeed store list price as seen in search snapshot (also reported by CNX Software 2024-09); the direct product page could not be fetched today, confirm before ordering. Module not included.

specs.power_input_connector: 2-pin terminal block (24 V / 5 A adapter included)
specs.can_controller: Orin MTTCAN (Linux SocketCAN can0/can1, module mttcan)
specs.can_transceiver: 3PEAK TPT71044-SOBR, isolated (pin-compatible with TI ISO1042BDWR), 1 W isolated 5 V supply B0505S-1WR3
specs.can_connector: J25, 2x10 3.81 mm pluggable terminal (YL032-096-020), shared with 4 DI / 4 DO
specs.can_pinout: CAN0_H pin 17, CAN0_L pin 19, CAN1_H pin 18, CAN1_L pin 20, GND_ISO pins 14 and 16
specs.can_termination: 120 ohm per channel, on by default, switched by GPIO through a CPC1017N PhotoMOS (CANx_120R_EN low = on)
specs.digital_io: 4 DI (12 V, optically isolated), 4 DO (40 V max, 40 mA per pin)

notes: Two isolated CAN-FD buses go straight to the motors with no USB adapter. The datasheet and getting-started spec table say '1x CAN', but the interfaces wiki and the v1.0 schematic (sheet 22/23) show two channels, CAN0 and CAN1, both brought out on J25. Tie motor-side CAN GND to GND_ISO. Absolute max input is 36 V, so 8S LiPo (33.6 V full) is the highest pack that can feed it directly; 10S and above needs a DC-DC. Linux on the Jetson is not hard real time, so use these ports for high-level commands and telemetry, or run the balance loop on an MCU (see research/power-electronics.md).
